| [ADR-109](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-109.md) v2 | The record keeps its research opportunities as LEADs, plans to advance a question or claim by any method, with a status for whether each is still worth following and a stage for how far it is worked out; and a question may presuppose another | The record's research opportunities were scattered: proposed-study CASEs (54, 28 of them bearing on no question), "What would answer it?" prose on 264 of 451 open questions, and proposed tests in dated notes. Nothing said which were still wanted, how far each was worked out, or which waited on which, and an opportunity that was not an experiment had no form at all. The owner asked on 2026-11-19 for a better way to represent this backlog, and supported dependencies among questions. A new scheme, LEAD, holds a plan to advance a question or claim: by reading, conceptual or formal work, a study, a history, or working out how a question could be advanced at all. Its status (Open, Done, Dropped, Superseded) says whether it is still worth following; a separate `stage` (idea, specified, underway) how far it is worked out. It `advances` questions and claims, may be `operationalized_in` a CASE that holds its design, and may `presuppose` a lead or a question. Questions gain `presupposes`, after THEORY's ([ADR-029](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-029.md)). Rejected: a "What would advance it?" section on every question; decision gates on claims; more fields on CASE; a backlog file outside the record. | Active — Amended by ADR-111 (2026-11-20): a priority and a blocked_on note, a costed stage after specified, advances widened to readings and terms, and the converse blurbs corrected. |
| [ADR-111](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-111.md) v2 | LEADs get a priority for triage and a blocked_on note; the stage ladder separates a specified design from a costed one; a lead may advance a reading or a term as well as a question or claim; and derived converses are stated as computed, not stored | Carries out recommendations 1 to 5 of [POSTMORTEM-002](../../../record/postmortems.d/POSTMORTEM-002.md), the review of [ADR-109](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-109.md) after the backlog audit filed 184 leads. A `priority` (high, medium, low) for triage, backfilled from the audit's ratings (59 high, 125 medium). The stage `specified` no longer needs a cost, which no source gave; a new stage `costed` holds what does; 53 leads whose design is in a CASE move from idea to specified, and one to costed. A plain `blocked_on` field says what a lead waits on that the record cannot do; two reading leads carry one. `advances` may name a THEORY (a replication that would meet its promote_when) or a TERM (the operationalization it waits on), with `advanced_by` derived on both. The blurbs of the derived converses now say they are computed for every reader and never stored, which is how luria treats a directed pair; they had said they were written by `luria link --fix`. QUESTION `presupposes` is kept, unused, until a sweep of question dependencies. Rejected: sorting the index by priority in place of line; a `blocked` status; dropping question dependencies; storing the converses. | Active |

| [ADR-136](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-136.md) v2 | An argument's title names its route, its grounds and the step, before its conclusion, and a Rejected argument says where its conclusion's own standing lives, so that rejecting a route is not read as rejecting what it concludes | At the owner's objection of 2026-11-21 to [ARG-142](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-142.md), whose title stated a conclusion ("the behaviour of sloppy models carries over to overparameterized neural networks") and whose status, Rejected, judged only one route to it: "marking it rejected predisposes future inquiry to treat that conclusion (which I think is actually probably correct) as rejected, rather than this particular path to that conclusion as rejected." Under [ADR-061](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md) an argument's status is a verdict on the inference, not the conclusion, but its title, which the index shows, did not say so. Decided: a title leads with the grounds and the step ("X, by analogy, shows that Y"), never the bare conclusion; a Rejected argument's summary says where the conclusion's own standing lives, in the claim or question that holds it, or that no entry holds it; and an untouched conclusion with content of its own is held in an entry of its own. One of two alternatives filed together; the other, [ADR-138](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-138.md), makes the title state the verdict instead. The assistant leans to this one. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [ADR-138](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-138.md) v2 | An argument's title states the record's verdict on its route, and a route the record finds fails is an Active argument titled that its grounds do not show its conclusion | The alternative to [ADR-136](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-136.md), filed together at the owner's objection of 2026-11-21 that a Rejected argument titled with its conclusion "predisposes future inquiry to treat that conclusion … as rejected, rather than this particular path to that conclusion". Here the title states the record's verdict: a route the record finds fails is filed as an Active argument titled "X does not show that Y", and one it accepts as "X shows that Y". Status then says whether the record holds its own judgement, as for any entry. This changes [ADR-061](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md)'s convention that "X does not show Y" is the argument from X to Y, Rejected, and needs a sweep of every held argument's status. It shares the other alternative's rule that an untouched conclusion is held on its own. The assistant leans to [ADR-136](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-136.md). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Rejected |
